Indikator 4a3 measures the proportion of patients with atrial fibrillation who receive anticoagulation treatment five years after their index date, evaluated across Danish regions and health clusters [^src1]. The established quality standard for this indicator requires a proportion of ≥ 90% [^src1]. 

In the current reporting period, the national average for [[danmark|Danmark]] was 87.3%, meaning the country as a whole missed the target [^src1]. Only four specific entities successfully met the ≥ 90% standard in the table data: [[klynge-nord|Klynge NORD]] led the comparison with 94.1%, followed by [[sundhedsklynge-sydvestjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sydvestjylland]] (91.6%), [[goedstrupklyngen|Gødstrupklyngen]] (91.5%), and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] (91.1%) [^src1]. All other regions and clusters fell short of the threshold [^src1]. Among the major regions, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] performed best at 89.3%, while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] trailed at 84.3% [^src1].

The lowest-performing entities overall were [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] at 80.0%, [[sundhedsklynge-midt|Sundhedsklynge Midt]] at 83.0%, and [[sundhedsklynge-byen|Sundhedsklynge Byen]] at 83.4% [^src1]. 

Although this comparison is drawn from a single dated section, the table includes historical data for the 2017/18 and 2016/17 periods, revealing notable shifts for certain clusters [^src1]. Most strikingly, [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] experienced a severe decline, dropping from 93.0% in 2017/18 to 80.0% in the current period [^src1]. In contrast, [[goedstrupklyngen|Gødstrupklyngen]] demonstrated steady improvement, rising from 86.8% in 2016/17 to 91.5% currently [^src1]. The national average fluctuated modestly, moving from 85.9% in 2016/17 to 88.1% in 2017/18, before settling at 87.3% [^src1].

For broader context on other cardiovascular indicators, historical data, and regional performance metrics across the Danish healthcare system, comprehensive analyses are documented throughout the 2023 and 2024 AFDK reports [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src14] [^src15] [^src16] [^src17] [^src18] [^src19].
